principles: Fix the real bug, never silence the detector (no re-allowlisting a live site).
Plain-repo byte-identity is non-negotiable: fall back to root when no gitRoot resolves.
One site at a time, re-verify the contract green after each (systematic debugging).
Prioritize the 3 hard failures; everything else is graceful-but-wrong.
Keep blast radius auditable: each fixed site is removed from the allowlist; the remaining allowlist is honestly split into permanent-benign vs explicitly-tracked-pending.
drivers: 3 deferred sites HARD-FAIL on wrapper-root (same class as the done-oracle DONE false-block already fixed) and must be fixed.
The contract is now in root npm test (B-99b6) so any regression fails validate immediately.
Blast radius spans ~16 production files; a per-site systematic approach bounds risk.
Most call sites lack store/storyId/config in scope, so the resolver must be threaded from callers or the id-independent resolveProjectGitRoot used.

options.name: A: full burndown (chosen)
pros: Shrinks the deferred set to only truly-benign entries
Fixes all 3 hard failures + graceful sites + lexical renames
Contract's standing exceptions become honest (benign vs empty pending)
cons: Requires threading deps through several caller chains

options.name: B: fix only the 3 hard failures + renames + allowlist split
pros: Still removes the only crash-class sites
cons: Leaves graceful-but-wrong sites in a named pending set (incomplete burndown)

options.name: C: revert B-6666 contract strengthening
cons: Loses the only mechanism that catches this whole bug class — rejected

rationale: Chosen A because the explicit charter is to burn the deferred list down to only truly-benign entries, and the triage proved the deferred set hides 3 hard wrapper-root failures plus several graceful-but-wrong sites. A is executed with the systematic one-site-at-a-time guardrail (rebuild + contract-smoke after each) which bounds the large blast radius, and falls back to B (3 hard failures + renames + allowlist split, graceful sites become a clearly-named tracked pending set with a B-id) ONLY if blast radius proves unsafe — never leaving the contract red or a hard-failure unfixed. C is rejected outright.

preMortem.scenario: An implementer silences a still-broken site by re-adding it to the allowlist instead of threading the resolver, making the contract green while the wrapper-root bug persists.
preMortem.trigger: Contract goes red after a partial fix and the fastest path back to green is re-allowlisting.
preMortem.consequence: The exact anti-pattern this whole effort fights returns; the deferred set never actually shrinks.
preMortem.mitigation: Hard rule in every implementer prompt + reviewer check: a site is removed from the allowlist ONLY after resolveGitCwd/resolveProjectGitRoot is threaded; re-allowlisting a real site is a critical finding. The pending set must end EMPTY (or hold only explicitly-tracked-with-B-id follow-ups).

preMortem.scenario: Threading the resolver changes the cwd on a PLAIN repo (projectRoot==gitRoot), breaking previously-working behavior.
preMortem.trigger: resolveGitCwd/resolveProjectGitRoot returns something other than the original root, or a fallback path is missed.
preMortem.consequence: Regression on the common (plain-repo) case — far more users than wrapper-root.
preMortem.mitigation: resolveGitCwd already returns projectRoot when unresolved; resolveProjectGitRoot returns null → caller MUST `?? root`. Every site keeps an explicit root fallback; reviewers verify plain-repo byte-identity; the contract self-tests + repo scan stay green.

preMortem.scenario: A caller chain lacks store/storyId/config, so the implementer fabricates a wrong storyId or skips resolution, silently resolving to the wrong worktree.
preMortem.trigger: A helper only has `root` and the implementer wants to use the storyId-keyed resolveGitCwd anyway.
preMortem.consequence: Wrong-worktree git operations (e.g. doctor --repair removing the wrong worktree) — worse than the original bug.
preMortem.mitigation: Use the id-independent resolveProjectGitRoot for no-storyId/project-level scans; only use resolveGitCwd where a REAL store+storyId is genuinely in scope at the caller. Thread deps from the caller, never invent an id. Wrapper-root regressions assert the resolved cwd is the gitRoot, not a guessed path.

preMortem.scenario: The allowlist split mislabels a still-unfixed real site as permanent-benign, hiding it forever.
preMortem.trigger: Sorting 28 entries into benign vs pending under time pressure.
preMortem.consequence: A real wrapper-root bug is permanently masked under the benign rationale.
preMortem.mitigation: Each BENIGN_BOOTSTRAP entry keeps its self-bootstrap/no-story-context rationale; any deferred graceful site goes in a clearly-named pending set with a B-id, never silently into benign; reviewer cross-checks every moved entry against whether it was actually fixed.
